name: Lights, Camera, Laundering!

pick.label: Pick a front
pick.heading: Pick a front and pitch the film
lead: In crime films, dirty money always hides somewhere boring: a car wash, a bar, a little shop that never seems to have any customers but somehow makes a fortune.
Choose a business from the shelf, or your own, and pitch a film about the money hiding behind it. *You need a scheme, a villain, a hero and a twist.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: This doesn't have to be realistic: no bank would fall for most film plots. It just has to be a film people would watch on a Sunday night. The sillier the better.

rows: Roughly! Fake customers, invoices for things that never happened, very expensive ice cream…
Who is really in charge, and why does nobody suspect them?
An auditor, a bank clerk, a nosy neighbour, a bored intern? What was the first red flag?

values.scheme: A dog salon in Friedrichshain that charges €900 for a “luxury poodle cut” and has sixty bookings a day. The whole street has about four dogs.
values.villain: Baron von Fluff, the salon's very calm poodle, who sits next to the till all day. Nobody suspects a dog.
values.hero: A tax inspector who lives upstairs and can't sleep. She counts the dogs from her balcony for three weeks and gets to eleven. They're all the same dog in different hats.
values.twist: The poodle really is in charge. His owner just signs whatever he barks at.
values.title: “The Poodle Job”: Every cut is a clean cut.
